plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors or their strategies. This is because you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid, so overbidding risks winning and paying more than the item is worth, while underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. With no prior history to suggest otherwise, I will bid exactly my value of $24 to maximize expected profit.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction, where bidding one's true value is the dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors or their strategies. Since I don't win-or-lose based on my own bid amount directly but rather pay the second-highest bid if I win, bidding exactly my value ensures I never overpay (I only win when profitable) and never miss profitable wins. Therefore, I will bid my true value of $9.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction with 3 bidders. In second-price auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy - it maximizes expected profit regardless of what others bid. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid (not my own), so overbidding risks negative profit, and underbidding risks losing profitable auctions. With my value at $13, I should bid exactly $13 to ensure I only win when profitable and capture maximum surplus when I do.
